chunks: Indeed, we — the community of the Progeny of Muhammad — wear al-Khazz and the Yemeni (cloth).

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The progeny/family of Muhammad — refers to the Ahl al-Bayt, the household of the Prophet
key_terms.الْخَزَّ: Al-Khazz — a luxury fabric woven from a mixture of silk and wool or other fibers; its permissibility is a point of jurisprudential discussion
key_terms.الْيُمْنَةَ: Yemeni cloth — fine striped cloth traditionally woven in Yemen, widely prized in the early Islamic world
key_terms.مَعَاشِرَ: Community/group of — used to indicate a collective identity sharing the same characteristics

ai.seo_question: Did the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt wear silk or al-Khazz fabric? What is the ruling on wearing al-Khazz in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) affirms that the Ahl al-Bayt, the progeny of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), wear al-Khazz — a fabric made from silk mixed with other fibers — along with Yemeni cloth. This narration serves as a legal testimony establishing the permissibility of wearing al-Khazz for Muslims, countering any prohibition based on the use of pure silk. The Imam speaks in the first person plural, establishing this as the recognized practice of the Prophetic household.
